forms.storage: After mixing with water, follow the label: many antibiotic suspensions must be kept in the fridge and thrown away after 7 to 10 days.
Shake liquid medicines well and measure with the cup or spoon that comes with them, not a kitchen spoon.
Do not let the dropper touch the eye or ear. Most drops must be thrown away 4 weeks after opening.
Keep unopened insulin in the fridge (not the freezer). The pen in use can stay at room temperature for about 4 weeks.
Keep effervescent tablets tightly closed in their tube; moisture spoils them.
Keep suppositories in a cool place so they don't melt.
Keep the inhaler away from heat and direct sunlight. Never puncture it.

storage: Keep medicines in a cool, dry place below 30°C, away from direct sunlight. Do not leave them in a hot car or on a window sill.
Keep all medicines out of reach of children.
Keep medicines in their original pack so you can see the name and expiry date.
